targetAudience.primary: Engineers building agent tool-approval, risk-classification and authorization caches
targetAudience.knowledgeAssumption: The reader understands approval workflows, cache keys, revocation and concurrent execution.
targetAudience.readerProblem: A recent low-risk classification can be reused after the user's governing authorization changes, especially when revocation races an in-flight classifier.

whyNow: A same-day merged OpenAI Codex Guardian v2 change binds cached low-risk scores to local and optional root authorization versions and revalidates the identity immediately before fast approval.

externalHook.description: Cached approval evidence becomes stale when its recorded authorization identity no longer equals the current one, including an in-flight race.

coreProposition: Reusable approval evidence should be bound to the authorization identity under which it was produced and revalidated immediately before it becomes execution authority; recency and action identity alone cannot make a cache revocation-aware, while version equality proves only the authority dimensions encoded by that version.

originalValue.description: Treats a cached classifier result as evidence produced under a particular authority identity, not as a time-limited permission token, and makes consumption-time revalidation the decisive safety boundary.

readerTakeaway: Key reusable approval evidence by action, risk, time and authority identity; recompute the represented authority at consumption, and fall back to review when it differs.

supported: The merged change defines a structured authorization version from selected conversation and host-produced input facts.
Successful cached scores record local and optional root authorization identity.
The fast-approval path recomputes current authorization and rejects mismatch, including an in-flight authorization change.
unsupported: Signed durable audit or distributed principal consistency
uncertain: Which external policy and tool-configuration identities should enter the version
How cached evidence should survive fork, resume and cross-process recovery

firstPartyRole.rationale: The article develops a general revocation-aware approval-cache pattern without relying on a first-party project.

decisionReason: The merged implementation and race regression support a concrete mechanism and a useful engineering rule while leaving classifier, tuple-completeness and effect-time claims bounded.
